elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: Operations delete p0025–p0029 in full; the rendered clause is empty, so no "Termination Payment" obligation of "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment" survives.

elements.element: No penalty or early-termination charge payable by Customer (including the trailing-Net-Sales formula)
elements.evidence: The formula "aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two" is deleted entirely.

elements.element: No residual payment mechanic imposing the amount on Customer
elements.evidence: Sub-paragraph (c) "payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments" is also deleted, leaving no dangling payment schedule.

elements.element: An early-termination fee exists as the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No exit charge remains anywhere in the redlined clause (clause deleted in full).

elements.element: Such fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No cap language is inserted; the fallback's "capped at 3 months' fees" appears only in the non-operative comment ("we can discuss one capped at three months' fees").

reasons: Locked target is preferred, and the preferred position is fully achieved: the entire Termination Payment obligation payable by the Company (our client) is removed, so no liquidated damages or early-termination penalty is payable by Customer.

Minimality is satisfied notwithstanding the official whole-paragraph gate: the offending operative content is the clause itself, and sub-paragraphs (b) (zero-floor rule) and (c) (eight quarterly instalments) are purely dependent mechanics that would become dangling references to an undefined "Termination Payment" if retained. No narrower operator, number, or phrase edit could eliminate the charge.
No new language, exception, or boilerplate was added, so there are no extra words to quote.

Untouched terms remain effective: Section 4.1's term, automatic renewal, 90-day notice and "Termination Date" definition are unaffected, and nothing else in the Agreement is left depending on the deleted "Termination Payment" definition.

Fallback is not met (no 3-month capped exit fee is inserted), but that is irrelevant here because the stricter preferred bargain is achieved in full; the fallback is correctly offered only in the margin comment.
The edit benefits our party and does not duplicate protection elsewhere.
